$comment: ARAP CPU runtime — the single source of truth for every pin in this image.
The Dockerfile reads it, the proofs assert against it, and
src/lib/__tests__/arapRuntimePins.test.ts fails if it drifts from
arapProvider.ts's ARAP_L3_RUN spec. A pin is a measurement, never a memory:
every sha256 below was computed by streaming the asset, and the provenance

image.role: standalone worker-runtime artifact — NOT referenced by story-worker.yml

base.why: 3.10 is the interpreter the ENV A recipe was measured on (mmcv-full 1.6.2 / mmdet 2.28.2 / mmpose 0.29.0 against torch 1.13.1). Debian bookworm carries libosmesa6 and libglu1-mesa, which ENV B needs. One interpreter, two venvs: isolation is the venv, not the python.

autorig.role: ENV A — drawn-humanoid detection + pose estimation + silhouette. Produces char_cfg.yaml / texture.png / mask.png.

no_fallback_why: MEASURED 2026-09-02: PyPI holds NO cpu-only torch 1.13.1 for linux
x86_64 — the only manylinux wheel is torch-1.13.1-cp310-cp310-manylinux1_x86_64.whl
at 887450534 bytes, which is the CUDA 11.7 build. The +cpu local version
exists ONLY on PyTorch's own index, download.pytorch.org.
The '+cpu' local version in the spec is the structural guarantee: PyPI
cannot satisfy it at all, so a reachability failure on the PyTorch index
STOPS the build instead of silently substituting the 887 MB CUDA wheel.
That substitution is the failure mode this pin exists to make impossible.
torch.hash_pin_why: torch is the ONLY asset here not hash-pinned in advance, because download.pytorch.org answers 403 CONNECT under this container's network policy and its wheels could not be streamed and hashed like the .mar models were. The first CI build RECORDS the sha256 pip reports and stamps the image hash_pinned:false; copying those hashes in here and rebuilding moves torch to ENFORCE, where a changed wheel fails the build. Until then torch is version-pinned only — which is fail-closed against a CUDA substitution but is NOT reproducibility, and must not be described as it.

mmcv_build.why: MEASURED 2026-09-02: download.openmmlab.com answers 403 CONNECT under this project's network policy, and PyPI ships mmcv-full 1.6.2 as an sdist only (no cp310 wheel). Source is the only route, and it must build against the ALREADY-INSTALLED cpu torch — hence --no-build-isolation.

autorig.mmpose_no_deps_why: mmpose 0.29.0 pulls chumpy, which is 3D-mesh only and does not build on numpy 1.23.5. The auto-rig uses the 2D top-down path.
autorig.xtcocotools_rebuild_why: Its published wheel is compiled against a different numpy ABI; rebuilt from source so it links numpy 1.23.5.
autorig.cython_why: MEASURED 2026-09-02: with --no-build-isolation pip provisions no build environment, so the pycocotools/xtcocotools source builds get no Cython and die on a missing generated _mask.c. Pinned because it is a build input like any other.

arap.role: ENV B — BVH retarget, ARAP 2D deform, headless OSMesa render. Consumes ENV A's character dir, produces the clip.
arap.no_torch_why: animated_drawings.render needs OpenGL, numpy, scipy, skimage and shapely — not torch. Keeping torch out of ENV B is the reason the split exists, and is what lets the two numpy pins coexist.

measured.note: Every version below is a `pip freeze` of the environment that actually produced the render recorded in `validation`.

arap.numpy_pin_why: 1.26.4, not AD's own 1.24.4 and not 2.x: AD's retarget stack uses np.bool8, which numpy 2 removed. arapProvider.ts records the same pin as ArapL3RunSpec.numpyPin.

system.ffmpeg_why: l3_animate_reference.py writes a gif; the host muxes to mp4 because OpenCV's h264 encoder is not always present.

animated_drawings.license_provenance: LICENSE read directly from raw.githubusercontent.com; repo archived read-only since 2025-09, so HEAD is stable.

assets.$comment: Every sha256 here was computed 2026-09-02 by streaming the asset through sha256sum in this container. None is quoted from memory.

drawn_humanoid_detector.mar.license_provenance: AnimatedDrawings README: 'Model weights are released under MIT license'. The .mar files were generated with OpenMMLab (mmdetection Apache-2.0). Recorded in OSS_MODEL_LICENSES.md as VERIFIED.
drawn_humanoid_detector.mar.url_provenance: Read from AnimatedDrawings' own torchserve/Dockerfile at the pinned commit, not composed by hand.

drawn_humanoid_pose_estimator.mar.license_provenance: As above (mmpose Apache-2.0 framework, weights MIT).
drawn_humanoid_pose_estimator.mar.url_provenance: Read from AnimatedDrawings' own torchserve/Dockerfile at the pinned commit.

u2netp.onnx.license_provenance: OSS_MODEL_LICENSES.md — rembg code VERIFIED MIT; U^2-Net weights recorded as Apache-2.0, marked UNVERIFIED there.
u2netp.onnx.why_mandatory: MEASURED: AD's classical threshold mask FAILED on 6/6 ONIQ painterly cast sheets (100% fill). arapProvider.ts records mask: 'rembg-u2netp' for this reason.
u2netp.onnx.url_provenance: Read from remotion/scripts/segment_reference.py's recorded setup block.

validation.$comment: What has actually been proven, and where. Anything not listed here is PENDING, not passing.

env_b_render.where: this container, 2026-09-02, natively on /usr/bin/python3.10 (no docker daemon is available here)
env_b_render.reads: Headless OSMesa GL, the arm-damped retarget config, the zombie.bvh WALKING driver and the ARAP deform all produce real, moving pixels on CPU with no display and no GPU.

read_only_nonroot_render.setup: AnimatedDrawings checkout chmod -R a-w, reached through the symlink view entrypoint.sh's ad_view() builds
read_only_nonroot_render.reads: The runner writes its scene config into the VIEW, not the checkout, so /opt/oniq can stay read-only to uid 10001 and a job cannot rewrite the code it runs. Verified as a non-root uid because root ignores permission bits — an earlier run as root passed while writing straight through a stale symlink into the read-only tree, and proved nothing.

env_a_stack.why: ENV A needs torch 1.13.1+cpu from download.pytorch.org, which answers 403 CONNECT under this container's network policy (measured 2026-09-02, agent-proxy recentRelayFailures). It is reachable from a GitHub Actions runner, so the build is CI's to do. No claim is made about ENV A until the publish workflow's proofs pass.

image_build.why: No docker daemon in this container (/var/run/docker.sock absent, measured 2026-09-02). The image cannot be built or benchmarked here.

benchmark_200_frame.why: Runs inside the built image, against the same 4-core shape the reference figures came from.

torch_hash_pin.status: PENDING — first CI build records the hashes
torch_hash_pin.why: See envs.autorig.torch.hash_pin_why. The build prints RECORD-ONLY lines; those hashes go into envs.autorig.torch.wheels and the next build enforces them.
